newsitem.title: USA: Missing half of barge found, towed to safety.
newsitem.headline: Missing half of barge found, towed to safety.

text.p: Crew members of a tug last week completed most of their 800-mile voyage from Alaska's Prince William Sound to British Columbia when they noticed that something was missing -- half of the barge they had been towing.

The back half of the 400-foot (122 metre) barge broke off somewhere around Kayak Island, southeast of Prince William Sound, said Coast Guard Lt. Commander Joe McGuiness of the agency's Valdez marine safety office.

The mishap went undiscovered until four days later, when crewmen from another vessel notified the tug of "structural damage" to the towed barge, which was carrying empty Alaska Railroad cars, McGuiness said.

"From the guys on the tug's point of view, it's extremely possible to go that long before you realise something is wrong," McGuiness said. "You can see the first few cars in the railroad, and you just don't see the caboose."
Just why the barge broke cleanly in half during a period of calm weather is a mystery, McGuiness said. "The Coast Guard will do an investigation on it," he said.
The lost barge half was found over the weekend drifing near the entrance of Prince William Sound. It was safely in port Monday, after being towed to Whittier Sunday, McGuiness said.
No railroad cars dropped into the sea from the drifing barge half, he said. "Isn't that amazing?" he said.
The tug is owned by Seattle-based Crowley Marine Services.
